F001.acceptance: (1) agent_brief renders deterministic text from live manifest and executor registry data. (2) Brief contains the operator-vs-worker distinction. (3) Brief warns that DontPanic orchestration is local CLI workflow orchestration, not Kubernetes/Airflow/IT orchestration. (4) Brief lists current supported commands from agent_manifest, including agent and orchestrate after F002. (5) Brief lists current worker executors from AGENT_REGISTRY and does not include unsupported labels. (6) Brief exposes generator version and content hash. (7) Tests mutate fake command/executor inputs and prove the rendered brief updates from source data.

F002.acceptance: (1) `dontpanic agent brief` prints the generated brief and exits 0. (2) `dontpanic agent status` classifies current/named agents as operator-only or worker-capable from AGENT_REGISTRY and role config. (3) `dontpanic agent setup grok` explains that Grok can operate DontPanic but cannot be registered as a worker without an executor. (4) `dontpanic agent register-worker <unknown>` refuses without writing config; `register-worker claude/codex` writes only valid role config according to the selected flags. (5) `dontpanic orchestrate` with no args prints the brief/workflow and exits 0 or 2 with actionable text, per existing CLI convention selected in implementation. (6) `dontpanic orchestrate <plan>` forwards to dispatch-from-plan without changing dry-run semantics. (7) `dontpanic orchestrate <plan> --confirm` reaches the same path as `dispatch-from-plan <plan> --confirm`. (8) `dontpanic manifest show/init` includes agent and orchestrate in supported_commands. (9) Tests cover the gateway and do not invoke real agent CLIs.

F003.acceptance: (1) `dontpanic projects add NAME PATH --onboard --dry-run` reports all intended writes without changing files. (2) `--onboard` creates `.dontpanic/dontpanic.json` with explicit defaults and a schema-compatible shape. (3) Missing AGENTS.md is created with the generated brief block. (4) Existing AGENTS.md content outside markers remains byte-for-byte unchanged. (5) Stale managed block is updated in place when hash/version differ. (6) Fresh managed block is left unchanged. (7) CLAUDE.md is created or updated as a pointer/alias without clobbering existing content. (8) Tests cover JSON and human output.

F004.acceptance: (1) A human or interactive agent can list available worker executors and current effective role assignments without reading JSON. (2) Assigning `auditor codex --project myrepo` writes the project roles block and leaves global config untouched. (3) Assigning `implementer claude --global` writes the global roles block. (4) Dry-run previews the exact file and value change. (5) Unknown executor names such as Grok-Builder are refused before writes. (6) Output explains operator-only versus worker-capable when refusal happens. (7) Dashboard state includes enough structured data to render role pickers and safe mutation commands. (8) Tests cover role resolution source layers and mutation targets.

F005.acceptance: (1) `dontpanic doctor --agent` validates the machine onboarding layer and prints registered worker executors. (2) `dontpanic doctor --project NAME` validates one project and its managed onboarding block. (3) Unknown global `roles.*` values fail. (4) Unknown project `roles.*` values fail. (5) Legacy implementer/auditor validation still works. (6) Stale or missing managed repo block is reported with an exact `projects add --onboard` remediation. (7) Existing doctor tests remain compatible. (8) Tests prove `Grok-Builder` is flagged as unrunnable unless registered in AGENT_REGISTRY.

F006.acceptance: (1) Doctor surfaces split-brain ~/.dontpanic vs ~/.jarvis state with file-level details. (2) Reconcile dry-run prints an exact migration plan and writes nothing. (3) Reconcile confirm migrates non-conflicting legacy-only files into ~/.dontpanic. (4) agent-manifest.json ends up in the canonical home after reconcile. (5) Divergent config.json and projects.json are not silently merged. (6) Legacy read-through compatibility remains for old installs after migration. (7) Tests cover all classification states and write behavior in isolated homes.

F007.acceptance: (1) A blocked quota/cooldown case renders a recommended wait-until + redispatch action and a separate raise-ceiling/threshold alternative when applicable. (2) The guidance explicitly states remaining max_iterations and whether the next fix iteration is within cap. (3) Budget and iteration guidance appears in CLI output and dashboard ActionItems from the same typed ActionChoice data. (4) A signed_off volley paused at pre_merge shows the gate state; after pre_merge is cleared, guidance offers a no-paid-call finalization action instead of forcing a fresh paid dispatch. (5) Setup guidance tells humans/agents when to run projects add --onboard, doctor --agent, doctor --project, agent brief, or home reconcile. (6) Human-required output includes exactly one response-level dashboard affordance: active URL when running, start command when not running; individual choices do not repeat it. (7) Exact commands are emitted only when safe AND validated against the live CLI grammar. "Validated" means: every emitted exact_command is a runnable invocation with the correct subcommand and all required arguments (it must not exit 2 on a usage error), and it respects current state. Concretely: (7a) no redispatch/orchestrate command is emitted when the next fix iteration would exceed max_iterations (exhausted state offers close/finalize or human action, never a redispatch command); (7b) no bare `dontpanic resume <plan>` — resume commands must carry the required `--gate <name>` or `--all`; (7c) no bare `dontpanic reconcile` — it must name the `homes` subcommand (e.g. `dontpanic reconcile homes --dry-run`); (7d) any response-level dashboard affordance referenced by an ActionItem must actually be present in the rendered dashboard cache, not merely named in detail text; (7e) re-onboarding guidance for an already-registered project emits `projects add <name> <path> --onboard --force --yes` (a bare `--onboard` is invalid because the registry refuses an existing name without --force --yes). When a valid command cannot be formed, guidance says human action required (requires_human) with advisory text instead of emitting a bare or invalid command. (8) Tests cover at least nine decision states, including the Codex cooldown + max_iterations example, signed_off/pre_merge finalization, active/inactive dashboard hints, and dashboard-hint deduplication; tests must also assert each of 7a–7e directly (exhausted-iteration emits no redispatch command; resume carries --gate/--all; reconcile names homes; referenced dashboard affordance is present in the built cache; already-registered re-onboard carries --force --yes). (9) A signed_off-and-pre_merge-cleared feature can be finalized with zero paid agent calls: a `dontpanic finalize <plan> --feature <F>` command, or equivalent, consumes the existing signed_off auditor artifact plus cleared gate-state, writes or repairs `signoff-<plan>.json`, and flips only that feature's passes:true with evidence_refs pointing at the audit artifact. (10) The finalizer refuses without mutation if the latest audit verdict is not signed_off, if pre_merge is uncleared, or if no audit envelope exists, with distinct exit codes per case. (11) The finalizer is idempotent and never triggers `dispatch_volley` or any worker executor invocation. (12) Tests prove clean signed_off to passes:true with no executor invocation, refusal on needs_changes, refusal on uncleared pre_merge, missing-audit refusal, and idempotent re-run. (Scope, per D035 split: F007 covers the decision engine, exact_command validity (7a–7e), and the no-paid finalizer with their CLI + dashboard rendering. Live-path completeness — every setup/doctor guidance state reachable from BOTH `what-now` and the dashboard, and ActionItem IDs carrying feature_id so distinct features do not collapse — is delegated to F012 and is OUT OF SCOPE for F007.)

F008.acceptance: (1) A human or interactive agent can run one command (`dontpanic config inventory [--project NAME|PATH] [--format text|json]`) to see all relevant DontPanic configuration surfaces and their status. (2) Inventory covers global config, project config, registry, manifest, roles, runtime evidence, gates/protected paths, quota/caps/calibration, circuit breakers, notifications, dashboard, capabilities/adapters, MCP, environments/Firebase, secrets/auth, install snapshot/reconcile, PM-tool credentials, and generated state. (2b) Status is correct, not optimistic: e.g. a roles provider whose resolved implementer/auditor is not in AGENT_REGISTRY reports a non-ok status (invalid/unrunnable), never `ok`. (2c) The non-optimistic-status rule is a GENERAL invariant across EVERY provider, not a per-example fix: any provider whose underlying state is invalid, incomplete, or unrunnable reports a non-ok status — e.g. roles not in AGENT_REGISTRY, quota caps present but calibration absent, capabilities/adapters known-but-unconfigured, manifest present-but-unloadable, etc. A single parametrized test asserts, for EACH provider, that an invalid/incomplete underlying state yields a non-ok status (so the suite proves the invariant holds class-wide, not just for the roles example). (4) Optional integrations are labeled optional and do not block core use. (5) Safe edits route through existing commands; secrets/auth steps are human-required and never echo secret values. (5b) "Safe command" means VALIDATED: every non-null `safe_command` PASSES `command_validation.validate_command_tokens` (stripping the `dontpanic`/`python -m dontpanic_orchestrate` prefix); a build/start/serve command (e.g. `dashboard build`, `mcp serve`) is NOT an edit affordance and must not be emitted as an inventory item's safe_command. (7) The setup/update planner can emit ActionChoices or a draft DontPanic plan for incomplete setup/update work. (8) Tests cover at least ten inventory providers, secret-safe output, the non-ok-on-invalid-roles case, AND a round-trip asserting EVERY non-null safe_command passes validate_command_tokens. (Scope, per D037 split: F008 is the inventory model + providers + CLI + validated safe_commands + correct status. Dashboard Settings/Setup rendering, active/inactive dashboard-hint auto-detection, and edit-vs-action affordance distinction are delegated to F013 and are OUT OF SCOPE for F008.) (2d) Tight-scope close-out requirements: the patch touches NO dashboard/* or dashboard settings files (that is F013 scope) — a patch modifying dashboard/* fails this AC; the present-but-UNLOADABLE config provider reports non-ok; a TRIPPED circuit-breaker provider reports non-ok; and the parametrized invariant test uses REAL invalid-state inputs (an actually-unloadable config file and an actually-tripped breaker) that fail before the fix and pass after — not trivially-passing weak cases. (2e) The non-optimistic-status invariant is implemented as a SINGLE shared status-derivation helper applied uniformly by EVERY provider (not per-provider ad-hoc checks); a `--project NAME|PATH` selector that does not resolve reports a non-ok/error status and never silently falls back to machine-only inventory; and ONE exhaustive parametrized test asserts, for EVERY provider, that a representative invalid/incomplete/unrunnable underlying state yields a non-ok status — covering at minimum unloadable config files, a tripped breaker, quota caps-present-but-calibration-absent, quota-state missing/unreadable, global_config/roles defaults that are not runnable executors, unsupported roles, an invalid manifest, and stale onboarding — with the test failing before the shared helper is applied and passing after. Per-provider patches that satisfy only the listed examples do NOT meet this AC.

F009.acceptance: (1) Dispatch records a plan-run fingerprint BEFORE the plan/features are loaded into memory and before any paid agent call, so every later drift check compares against true dispatch-start disk state (AC1 + codex #2: baseline must precede the plan load at supervisor.py:1371, not follow it). (2) Plan changes during a run are detected before the next paid agent call or signoff finalization, on the VOLLEY dispatch path. (3) Additive decisions.jsonl drift is reconciled in-place without stopping, with an event recorded (AC3). (4) Feature/acceptance/gate/role/loop-cap drift PAUSES the volley (paused_on_drift) and tells the operator how to refresh/redispatch (AC4). (5) Drift detection FAILS CLOSED (codex #3): a fingerprint/reconcile error pauses or raises rather than swallowing the exception and continuing on possibly-stale context — a safety mechanism must not fail open. (6) Tests simulate another process editing plan files mid-run on the volley path and prove DontPanic does not continue on stale context silently, incl. a fail-closed test that the drift check raising does NOT silently proceed. (Single-agent dispatch coverage, scope/policy human-ack workflow, and CLI/dashboard one-action surfacing are SPLIT to F014 — D056.)

F010.acceptance: (1) Starting a second dashboard serve in the same DontPanic home refuses with an actionable message. (2) Stale singleton records are pruned. (3) `--replace` or equivalent intentionally replaces a live singleton. (4) Dashboard status helper returns active URL when running and start command when inactive. (5) Shared render helper emits the dashboard hint once per response even when many items require human input. (6) Existing bind failure handling still works. (7) Tests cover singleton behavior, status helper, and deduped hint rendering without opening a browser. (8) README and getting-started docs show the complete new-agent, new-repo, role-assignment, config-inventory/setup, budget/iteration guidance, skill invocation recommendation, and dashboard decision flow. (9) CHANGELOG documents the operator-visible changes. (10) Full targeted test suite passes.

F011.acceptance: (1) `SKILL.md` supports validated `invocation:` metadata without breaking skills that lack it. (2) The recommender emits typed SkillAction records from an injected pure SkillInvocationContext with recommendation values `auto_run`, `suggest`, `approval_required`, `blocked_missing_inputs`, and `not_applicable`. (3) Skills without invocation metadata are never auto-run. (4) Read-only bounded skills auto-run or become auto-runnable only when required inputs exist and the exact command is present in a versioned auditable auto-run allowlist. (5) The allowlist has owner/approval metadata, version/hash, rationale, and command template/prefix fields; doctor/reconcile and F008 config inventory expose missing/stale/conflicting allowlist state. (6) Risk precedence is deterministic and tested: explicit never-auto/never-suggest, external writes, paid actions, indefinite loops, credentialed production reads, network access, repo mutation, missing allowlist, and missing inputs downgrade/block auto-run regardless of declared mode. (7) Mutating, credentialed, networked, paid, external-write, or indefinite-loop skills require approval or are suggested; they are never silently executed. (8) Missing inputs produce one concise ActionChoice or dashboard action naming only the missing blocker. (9) CLI and dashboard render the same SkillAction data, including reason, risk, command, approval requirement, and evidence target. (10) The recommender uses F008 config inventory to explain unavailable credentials/binaries/capabilities and F007 dashboard-hint deduplication for human decisions. (11) Existing skills have a migration path: a rubric suggestion command or doctor advisory identifies high-value skills missing invocation metadata and proposes safe starting rubrics without blocking core use. (12) `never_suggest` or equivalent opt-out prevents noisy/toolkit skills from appearing in recommendations. (13) Representative current skills are covered by fixtures: autoresearch, security-review, eval-harness, test-runner, cost-model, changelog, browser-use, revenue-check, github-pr, worktree-isolation, subagent-driven-dev, prompt-optimizer, and printing-press-adapter. (14) Tests prove each recommendation class, no-auto fallback, never-suggest opt-out, command allowlist enforcement, risk precedence with contradictory metadata, missing-input handling, dashboard JSON shape, doctor/reconcile allowlist visibility, migration suggestion output, and no invocation of approval-required skills.

F012.acceptance: (1) `collect_state()` (the live path used by `dontpanic what-now` and the dashboard) derives every setup/doctor guidance state F007's builder emits: missing registration, stale onboarding, unsupported roles.*, doctor --agent, doctor --project, agent brief, and home reconcile — none are builder-only/unreachable. (2) `dontpanic what-now` renders each of those setup/doctor states with a validated exact_command (per F007 7a–7e) or a requires_human advisory when no safe command exists. (3) The dashboard renders the same setup/doctor ActionChoices as ActionItems, achieving CLI+dashboard parity for setup guidance. (4) Dashboard ActionItem IDs include feature_id so two distinct blocked features sharing a choice kind produce two distinct items; intentional plan-level blocker dedup is preserved. (5) Tests prove each setup/doctor state is reachable from BOTH what-now and the built dashboard cache, and that two same-kind blocked features yield two distinct ActionItems (no collapse). (6) "Validated exact_command" means the command actually PASSES `command_validation.validate_command_tokens` (not merely that a string matches): `command_validation.py` must recognize every command operations_guidance can emit across all states — including `agent brief`, `finalize <plan> --feature <F>`, `what-now <plan> --feature <F>`, `orchestrate <plan>`, `doctor --agent`, `doctor --project <name>`, `reconcile homes [--dry-run]`, and `projects add <name> <path> --onboard --force --yes`. Any state whose command does NOT pass the validator must emit `requires_human` advisory with `exact_command=None` instead of an invalid string. (7) A test iterates EVERY non-null `exact_command` emitted by `build_guidance`/`collect_state` across all quota/budget/iteration/finalize/setup/doctor states and asserts each passes `validate_command_tokens` (stripping the `dontpanic`/`python -m dontpanic_orchestrate` prefix) — this is what makes the green suite actually prove validity (closing the codex i2 gap where string-equality tests let invalid shapes through).

F013.acceptance: (1) The dashboard build renders the F008 inventory as Settings/Setup cards (same data the CLI `config inventory` shows), not merely a generated state blob. (2) The response-level dashboard_hint auto-detects a running dashboard singleton for active_url and falls back to the start command when none runs — without the caller manually passing dashboard_url. (3) Exactly one response-level dashboard_hint; item-level records reference it rather than repeating text. (4) Edit affordances (validated safe_command) are rendered distinctly from run-actions; build/start/serve commands never render as an item's edit safe_command. (5) Tests prove cards render for >=10 providers, active/inactive hint auto-detection, dashboard-hint dedup, and that no build/start command is emitted as an edit affordance.

F014.acceptance: (1) The single-agent dispatch path (cli.py dispatch_single_agent) is guarded by the SAME F009 drift reconciliation as the volley path — no paid single-agent call proceeds on stale plan context (codex F009 #4). (2) Blocking scope/policy drift (allowed_paths / forbidden_decisions, AC5) is enforced as a real human-acknowledgement workflow: the run pauses and requires an explicit operator ack (e.g. `dontpanic approve <plan> drift:<class>` or equivalent) before any further paid call — not merely labeled human_required in plan_drift.py (codex F009 #5). (3) CLI and dashboard show ONE concise reconciliation action, not repeated warnings (F009 AC6). (4) Tests cover: single-agent path pauses on blocking drift; the scope/policy ack workflow blocks-then-resumes; and the CLI/dashboard emit exactly one reconciliation action.

forbidden_decisions: Do not hand-maintain multiple copies of the operating brief.
Do not pretend unsupported interactive agents are dispatch executors.
Do not overwrite existing AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md content outside marked managed blocks.
Do not silently resolve contradictory ~/.dontpanic and ~/.jarvis state.
Do not add a Grok/Gemini/etc. executor label without a real executor implementation.
